counterfactual_missing_items: Acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli in distal main pulmonary arteries extending into lobar and segmental branches of upper and lower lobes bilaterally
Initial 12-lead electrocardiogram showed no evidence of acute myocardial ischemia or arrhythmias.
decisive_items: Acute extensive partially occlusive pulmonary emboli in distal main pulmonary arteries extending into lobar and segmental branches of upper and lower lobes bilaterally
Dilated right ventricle with RV-LV ratio >1.5
response.rationale: R1 is the only candidate directly anchored to the causative CT angiogram finding of acute bilateral pulmonary emboli, with supporting D-dimer elevation and RV strain. R6 captures the downstream pulmonary hypertension/RV failure but omits the embolic cause; R5 is a correlated restatement of RV failure without pulmonary hypertension; R2 is contradicted by the ECG and its troponin elevation is nonspecific.

rejected.why: Elevated troponin is nonspecific and explicitly contradicted by the ECG showing no acute ischemia or arrhythmias; PE explains the troponin rise.
Acute right ventricular failure is a downstream complication of PE, not the primary diagnosis, and lacks the direct embolic cause and pulmonary hypertension.
